title: Thiruparankundram Karthigai Deepam Row: Know The Legend Of Lord Shiva’s Infinite Flame
description: The Supreme Court's one-time permission to light a lamp at Thiruparankundram has reignited a religious row. Know all about the Karthigai ritual and Shiva's infinite flame legend.
author: Tanya Dutt
content:
Thiruparankundram Karthigai Deepam Row: Know The Legend Of Lord Shiva’s Infinite Flame
The Supreme Court's one-time permission to light a lamp at Thiruparankundram has reignited a religious row. Know all about the Karthigai ritual and Shiva's infinite flame legend.
The lighting of a traditional lamp at Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai has become the centre of a religious and legal dispute, bringing the centuries-old Karthigai Deepam festival into focus.
On November 20, 2026, the Supreme Court permitted the ceremonial lighting of a lamp at the disputed Deepathoon, a stone pillar on the hill, as a one-time measure for November 24. The order came amid a long-standing disagreement over the location of the ritual, with temple authorities and petitioners asserting different positions on its traditional significance. The Tamil Nadu government subsequently sought a review of the decision.
- Smart Entertainment on a Budget: 43-Inch TVs Under Rs 20,000 Tailored for Smaller Spaces
- Cigarettes for Shiva, Whisky for Bhairav, Toy Planes for Visas: India's Unusual Faith Traditions
- Dev Diwali 2026: Dev Deepavali Wishes, Images, Quotes And Messages To Share
- Karthigai Deepam 2026: Why Has Lighting A Lamp On A Tamil Nadu Hill Become A Matter For The Supreme Court?
The hill is also home to the Sulthan Sikkandar Avulia Dargah, making the dispute particularly sensitive. The Supreme Court’s interim order does not establish any permanent religious or customary right over the site.
The hill, home to the ancient Subramaniaswamy Temple (first of Murugan’s six abodes) and a nearby dargah, remains a complex sacred landscape.
What Is Karthigai Deepam?
Karthigai Deepam is an important Tamil Hindu festival celebrated during the Tamil month of Karthigai, which falls across November and December. The festival is also linked to Lord Murugan (Kartikeya), born from six sparks of Shiva’s third eye, nurtured by the six Krittika maidens and united by Parvati into the six-faced Arumugam.
The festival symbolises the triumph of light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance. Its most prominent celebration takes place at the Arunachaleswarar Temple in Tiruvannamalai, where a massive flame, known as Maha Deepam, is lit atop Annamalai Hill.
Across Tamil Nadu, families clean homes, draw kolams, and light rows of clay agal vilakku at dusk, symbolising the triumph of light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance.
At Tiruvannamalai’s Arunachaleswarar Temple, the Bharani Deepam is lit before dawn inside the shrine, followed by the grand Maha Deepam atop Annamalai Hill at sunset—a huge ghee-filled cauldron whose flame is visible for kilometres and represents Shiva as Arunachaleswarar. Devotees perform the 14-km Girivalam circumambulation of the sacred hill, often barefoot.
The Legend Of Lord Shiva’s Infinite Flame
According to Hindu mythology, Lord Brahma and Lord Vishnu once disagreed over who was the supreme deity. To settle their argument, Lord Shiva appeared before them as an enormous pillar of fire that extended infinitely into the heavens and beneath the earth.
Determined to discover its limits, Brahma transformed into a swan and flew upwards to find its summit. Vishnu took the form of a boar and dug into the earth to locate its base.
Despite their efforts, neither deity could find the beginning or end of the divine flame. Their search established that Lord Shiva was infinite, beyond the limits of human understanding and perception.
The legend is closely associated with Arunachala, the sacred hill at Tiruvannamalai, which devotees believe symbolises Lord Shiva himself.
Quick Answers
On November 20, 2026, the Supreme Court permitted the ceremonial lighting of a lamp at the disputed Deepathoon stone pillar as a one-time measure for November 24, restricting access exclusively to an authorised team from the Devasthanam and government officials.

title: Cabinet clears ₹6,302 crore for new Assam airport, Tamil Nadu port expansion
description: With an existing port terminal running near peak capacity and a regional airport hemmed in by defence land constraints, New Delhi’s latest multi-crore approval targets two critical logistics chokepoints, without straining the central exchequer for the bulk of the bill.
author: Sapna Das, Asmi Saxena
content:
Cabinet clears ₹6,302 crore for new Assam airport, Tamil Nadu port expansion
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 16:04 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 16:04 IST
With an existing port terminal running near peak capacity and a regional airport hemmed in by defence land constraints, New Delhi’s latest multi-crore approval targets two critical logistics chokepoints, without straining the central exchequer for the bulk of the bill.
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) on Wednesday approved two infrastructure projects involving an estimated investment of ₹6,302.26 crore, including a greenfield airport at Doloo in Silchar, Assam, and a second container terminal at Kamarajar Port in Tamil Nadu.
The airport project has been approved at an estimated cost of ₹2,014 crore, while the second container terminal at Kamarajar Port will involve an investment of ₹4,288.26 crore under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) model.
The proposed greenfield airport will be developed by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) at Doloo in Assam's Cachar district. The project is aimed at addressing operational and space constraints at the existing Silchar Airport, which operates from a defence land enclave, and accommodating rising passenger traffic.
The proposed airport will have a terminal building spanning 12,351 square metres, with the capacity to handle 800 passengers during peak hours. It will also include a 2,705-metre runway designed for A-320 aircraft, an apron with parking capacity for six A-320 aircraft and an isolation bay.
The airport is expected to improve air connectivity in the Barak Valley and neighbouring states, while supporting trade and tourism in the region.
Kamarajar Port to add 2 million TEUs of capacity
The Cabinet also approved the development of a second container terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited (KPL) in Tamil Nadu at an estimated project cost of ₹4,288.26 crore, including Goods and Services Tax (GST).
The terminal will be developed under the Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) model through a PPP arrangement. It will have a 900-metre-long berth, a design draft of 18 metres and an annual handling capacity of 2 million Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs).
The project will be executed in two phases. Phase I will add 1.1 million TEUs of capacity at an estimated cost of ₹2,429.32 crore, while Phase II will add another 0.9 million TEUs at a cost of ₹1,858.94 crore.
The terminal is designed to handle container vessels with capacities of up to 24,346 TEUs and lengths of up to 400 metres. It is expected to improve the port's ability to receive larger vessels and strengthen direct connectivity with international shipping routes.
The selected concessionaire will arrange the investment for the terminal under the DBFOT framework. Kamarajar Port will separately incur an estimated ₹450 crore towards dredging.
Also read: Mumbai's ₹53,928-crore 'Pataal Lok' project: Key facts about the underground road network
40-year concession, 48-month construction timeline
The container terminal project will have a concession period of 40 years, including a construction period of 48 months. Phase I is scheduled to be completed within 24 months of the award of the concession, with commercial operations expected to begin in the 25th month.
Construction of Phase II will take place between the 25th and 48th months, with the entire terminal expected to become operational in the 49th month.
The existing container terminal at Kamarajar Port has an installed capacity of 0.8 million TEUs per year and handled around 0.7 million TEUs in FY26, translating into capacity utilisation of approximately 88%.
The port handled 49.08 million tonnes of cargo and 1,008 vessels during FY26, including more than 7 lakh TEUs of container traffic. Its container traffic has grown at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of around 9.9% over the past five years, compared with growth of about 7% in India's container traffic.
The proposed terminal is expected to cater to export-import (EXIM) cargo demand from the Chennai-Ennore industrial region and the wider southern hinterland. The project is also expected to generate around 750 direct and indirect jobs during construction and increase employment by about 800 during the operational phase.
The government said the investment in the PPP component would be arranged by the selected concessionaire, with no financial implication for the Centre.

title: Over ₹100 crore suspected missing from Haryana panchayat accounts, govt orders statewide probe
description: Officials found that nearly 80% of the payments made after Diwali were not approved by the department. Police have so far frozen around ₹8 crore.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
Over ₹100 crore suspected missing from Haryana panchayat accounts, govt orders statewide probe
- Edited bySudarsanan M
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 15:55 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 15:55 IST
Haryana has launched a statewide audit following the massive unauthorised withdrawal of public funds bypassing digital approval systems. Investigators are probing banking vulnerabilities and freezing illicit transfers.
More than ₹100 crore is suspected to have been withdrawn from panchayat and other Panchayati Raj institutions' bank accounts in Haryana without proper authorisation. Now, the state government has ordered a wider audit of government accounts.
The suspected fraud came to light after officials found unauthorised transactions in several panchayat accounts. The Haryana Development and Panchayats Department has already ordered a forensic audit to determine how the transfers were made and whether the banking and payment systems had lapses.
The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) will carry out the audit, according to The Indian Express.
The report added that nearly ₹4.5 crore had been identified as missing from accounts of several Panchayati Raj Institutions.
ALSO READ | CERT-In warns of unauthorised payment transactions, AI-driven cyberattacks across sectors
Officials in Fatehabad and other districts have reported additional suspicious withdrawals, taking the suspected exposure to more than ₹100 crore as authorities expand their checks.
In Fatehabad, ₹87.48 lakh was transferred from the District Council's Punjab National Bank account through 14 NEFT transactions between November 10 and 15. Another ₹10 lakh was withdrawn from the Mehuawala gram panchayat account in Bhattu Kalan.
Fatehabad Zila Parishad chairperson Suman Khichar told The Indian Express that more than ₹80 lakh went missing from PRIs’ bank accounts in the district. He added, “We have informed the department about it.”
The suspected irregularities became particularly apparent when officials compared bank records with departmental records.
According to Dainik Jagran, nearly 80% of the payments made after Diwali were found to have not been approved by the department.
Police have so far managed to freeze around ₹8 crore out of suspected ₹100 crore, the report added.
ALSO READ | Maharashtra Cyber issues advisory against online fraud, urges citizens to stay alert
A key question is how the transactions were processed without the required authorisation. Haryana's Fund Disbursement Management System (FDMS) requires authorised officials to approve payments with digital signatures before sending instructions to the bank.
The department said that the disputed transactions were not generated or authorised through the FDMS, raising questions about how the payment instructions reached the banks.
Officials are examining several possible vulnerabilities, including incomplete KYC records, the absence of daily account reconciliation and possible weaknesses in the banking system. The department has also reported the matter to the Haryana Police Cyber Wing. A bank-level forensic investigation is also being pursued in connection with the transactions.
The investigation is now being widened beyond Panchayati Raj institutions. Haryana authorities have ordered checks of bank accounts belonging to government departments, boards, corporations and even courts to determine whether similar unauthorised transactions have occurred elsewhere.
The Finance Department has directed government bodies to recheck their electronic transactions with bank records daily and correct any discrepancies within 24 hours.
It has also stressed that the same person or system should not be responsible for both initiating and approving a payment.

title: Meta officials meet India's opposition Congress amid protests on content curbs: Report
description: Meta executives in India held closed-door talks with the opposition Congress party to defuse protests over content moderation and alleged favoritism toward the ruling BJP.
author: Reuters
content:
Meta officials meet India's opposition Congress amid protests on content curbs: Report
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 15:34 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 15:34 IST
Meta executives in India held closed-door talks with the opposition Congress party to defuse protests over content moderation and alleged favoritism toward the ruling BJP.
Meta’s top executives in India held closed-door talks with the country’s opposition Congress party as the two sides try to defuse protests against the US firm’s content moderation practices, four people familiar with the matter said.
Meta’s Aman Jain and Natasha Jog, two key executives in India, represented the company at the meeting at Congress headquarters on Tuesday, one person said.
They raised concerns about protests targeting Meta’s offices and the depiction of CEO Mark Zuckerberg in posters. Congress raised concerns about a rise in restrictions on its leaders’ accounts and posts, and about allegations that Meta favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), three other people said. Meta has denied any favouritism.
The meeting marked Meta’s first direct engagement with the party since protests by its youth wing began on Friday.
The Youth Congress has demanded that Meta restore accounts taken down on government orders and explain how its algorithms restrict posts, and its members have clashed with police near Meta’s offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram.
Congress did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while Meta said it moderates content in India in accordance with the law. Meta executives Jain and Jog did not respond.
Meta made no commitments to the party during the meeting and explained that it was bound by local laws, said one of the people, who had direct knowledge of the discussions. The executives also emphasised that Meta was neutral towards all political parties, the person said.
The dispute adds to political pushback for Meta in its biggest market by users, where it restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts under local laws in the first half of 2026, up from about 70,000 in all of 2025, company disclosures show.
Meta attributes the rise to India’s amended IT rules that require faster and more proactive takedowns, but it has triggered a debate over free speech as the government steps up demands to remove online content.
The protests took a fresh turn in recent days as posters and banners depicting Zuckerberg in a white shirt, khaki shorts and black cap, the traditional uniform of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), appeared in cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Patna, Mumbai and Bengaluru. The RSS is a Hindu nationalist volunteer organisation that is the ideological parent of the BJP.
”This is Congress Model: Vandalise offices of private companies,” BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari wrote on X on Saturday.

title: वक्फ बोर्ड के समारोह में 'वंदे मातरम' बजाने पर भड़का MMU, कहा- तौहीद और आस्था से समझौता नहीं
description: वक्फ बोर्ड के एक समारोह में 'वंदे मातरम' बजाए जाने को लेकर MMU ने कड़ी नाराजगी जताई है. संगठन ने स्पष्ट कहा कि तौहीद और धार्मिक आस्था के साथ किसी भी तरह का समझौता स्वीकार नहीं किया जाएगा. पढ़ें पूरा विवाद और प्रतिक्रियाएं.
author: रवींद्र प्रताप सिंह
content:
जम्मू-कश्मीर के विभिन्न इस्लामी संगठनों और धार्मिक संस्थाओं के प्रमुख मंच 'मुत्ताहिदा मजलिस-ए-उलेमा' (MMU) ने श्रीनगर में आयोजित वक्फ डे समारोह के दौरान 'वंदे मातरम' बजाए जाने पर कड़ा ऐतराज जताया है. जम्मू-कश्मीर वक्फ बोर्ड द्वारा आयोजित इस कार्यक्रम में हुए इस घटनाक्रम की निंदा करते हुए संगठन ने इसे मुस्लिम समाज की धार्मिक भावनाओं को आहत करने वाला कदम बताया है. साथ ही, एमएमयू ने राज्य के सरकारी कार्यक्रमों और शिक्षण संस्थानों में वंदे मातरम को कथित तौर पर अनिवार्य बनाए जाने पर गहरी चिंता व्यक्त करते हुए इसके खिलाफ कानूनी सलाह लेने और प्रशासन को औपचारिक ज्ञापन सौंपने का फैसला किया है.
एमएमयू ने इस बात पर गहरा अफसोस जताया कि यह घटना खुद वक्फ बोर्ड के कार्यक्रम में हुई है, जिसकी मुख्य जिम्मेदारी मुस्लिम धार्मिक संपत्तियों और उनकी पवित्रता की रक्षा करना है. संगठन के अनुसार, महज एक आधिकारिक कार्यक्रम होने के कारण वहां वंदे मातरम बजाने की कोई कानूनी बाध्यता नहीं थी और यह पूरी तरह से वैकल्पिक था. इसके बावजूद वक्फ बोर्ड ने कश्मीरी मुसलमानों की बुनियादी धार्मिक मान्यताओं और संवेदनाओं को नजरअंदाज करते हुए इसे बजाया, जिससे आम लोगों में गहरा दुख और रोष व्याप्त है. एमएमयू ने धार्मिक जिम्मेदारियों से जुड़े लोगों को याद दिलाया कि किसी भी पद, दबाव या स्वार्थ से ऊपर उठकर इस्लाम के बुनियादी सिद्धांतों की रक्षा करना उनका कर्तव्य है.
अपने बयान में एमएमयू ने इस्लाम के सबसे बुनियादी और अटल सिद्धांत 'तौहीद' (अल्लाह की एकत्वता) का हवाला देते हुए स्पष्ट किया कि इस्लाम में अल्लाह के साथ किसी भी व्यक्ति, वस्तु, भूमि या रचना को साझीदार ठहराना या उसे दैवीय दर्जा देना सख्त वर्जित है. संगठन ने कहा कि इस्लाम अपने वतन से मोहब्बत करने की शिक्षा तो देता है, लेकिन वतन से प्रेम करने और उसकी पूजा करने के बीच एक स्पष्ट रेखा खींचता है. मातृभूमि को दैवीय रूप देने वाली कोई भी अभिव्यक्ति या प्रथा तौहीद के खिलाफ है, इसलिए मुसलमानों के लिए यह अस्वीकार्य है. एमएमयू ने यह भी याद दिलाया कि ऑल इंडिया मुस्लिम पर्सनल लॉ बोर्ड (AIMPLB) भी पहले ही धार्मिक और संवैधानिक आधार पर वंदे मातरम की अनिवार्यता का कड़ा विरोध कर चुका है.
संगठन ने मुस्लिम बहुल जम्मू-कश्मीर के सरकारी आयोजनों में वंदे मातरम को लगातार शामिल किए जाने पर गंभीर चिंता जताई है. एमएमयू का मानना है कि मुसलमानों की सर्वविदित धार्मिक आपत्तियों के बावजूद इसे थोपना न केवल उनकी आस्था की अनदेखी है, बल्कि उनके संवैधानिक अधिकारों का भी हनन है. इस तरह के कदमों से समाज में अविश्वास और अलगाव की भावना और गहरी होती है.
मामले की गंभीरता को देखते हुए एमएमयू ने अब इस मुद्दे पर कानूनी विशेषज्ञों की राय लेने की प्रक्रिया शुरू कर दी है. संगठन जल्द ही संबंधित अधिकारियों को एक औपचारिक ज्ञापन सौंपकर मांग करेगा कि जम्मू-कश्मीर के सरकारी कार्यक्रमों, शिक्षण संस्थानों और अन्य सार्वजनिक आयोजनों में वंदे मातरम को जबरन लागू करने पर तत्काल रोक लगाई जाए. एमएमयू ने प्रशासन से संविधान द्वारा प्रदत्त धार्मिक स्वतंत्रता और अंतरात्मा की आजादी का सम्मान करने की अपील करते हुए दोहराया कि आस्था और 'तौहीद' के मामले में किसी भी तरह का समझौता संभव नहीं है.

title: पुणे कोर्ट के बाहर दिनदहाड़े गैंगवार! पेशी के लिए आए हत्या के आरोपी पर हमला, पहले चलाईं गोलियां फिर चापड़ से काटा हाथ
description: पुणे जिला अदालत के बाहर दिनदहाड़े हत्या के आरोपी मंदार किवाले पर हथियारबंद हमलावरों ने हमला कर दिया. चापड़ से उसका हाथ काट दिया गया. घटना में दो अन्य लोग घायल हुए हैं. पुलिस हमलावरों की तलाश कर रही है.
author: ताहिर कामरान
content:
पुणे के शिवाजीनगर में बुधवार को हुई एक खौफनाक घटना ने सभी को हैरान कर दिया है. यहां अदालत के बाहर हथियारबंद लोगों के एक समूह ने कथित तौर पर गोलीबारी की और दो लोगों पर दरांतियों से हमला कर दिया. इस घटना में दो लोग घायल हो गए. घायलों में से एक की हालत गंभीर है. बताया जा रहा है कि एक का हाथ कलाई से कटकर अलग हो गया है.
यह हमला दोपहर करीब 1 बजे फैमिली कोर्ट के सामने गेट नंबर 4 के पास हुआ. घटना के बाद वहां मौजूद लोगों और अदालत में आए फरियादियों के बीच अफरा-तफरी मच गई. शुरुआती जानकारी के मुताबिक, हमलावर दो दोपहिया वाहनों पर सवार होकर आए थे. उनके पास बंदूकें और दरांतियां थीं. पुलिस के मुताबिक, एक वाहन पर तीन और दूसरे पर चार लोग सवार थे. वहीं, चश्मदीदों ने हमलावरों की संख्या करीब छह बताई है.
आरोप है कि हमलावरों ने पहले गोलियां चलाईं और फिर पीड़ितों पर दरांतियों से हमला कर दिया. इसके बाद वे मौके से फरार हो गए. हमले में एक व्यक्ति के बाएं हाथ की कलाई पर गंभीर चोट आई. बताया जा रहा है कि उसका हाथ कलाई से कटकर अलग हो गया. वह बेहोशी की हालत में मिला और उसे तुरंत अस्पताल पहुंचाया गया. उसकी हालत गंभीर बताई जा रही है.
हमलावरों के फरार होने के बाद अदालत के गेट के बाहर से दो बंदूकें और इस्तेमाल किए गए कारतूस मिलने की जानकारी सामने आई है. जानकारी मिलते ही पुलिस की टीमें मौके पर पहुंचीं और पूरे इलाके की घेराबंदी कर दी. वरिष्ठ पुलिस अधिकारी और फॉरेंसिक टीम भी सबूत जुटाने के लिए घटनास्थल पर पहुंची. पुलिस अभी गोली चलाने वाले व्यक्ति की पहचान और हमले के पीछे की वजह का पता लगा रही है. साथ ही यह भी जांच की जा रही है कि हमला किसी खास व्यक्ति को निशाना बनाकर किया गया था या इसके पीछे कोई दूसरी वजह थी.

title: नशा तस्करी का विरोध, जान पर आई आफत: ATM जा रहे AAP सरपंच के पति पर दिनदहाड़े फायरिंग; पैर में गोली लगने से घायल
description: पंजाब के तरनतारन में एक महिला सरपंच और उसके पति पर हमला हुआ है. आरोप है कि सरपंच का परिवार नशे के खिलाफ मुहिम चला रहा था और गांव के ही कुछ लोगों को नशा बेचने से रोका था.
author: अभिनव त्रिपाठी
content:
पंजाब के तरतारन से एक हैरान करने वाला मामला सामने आया है. यहां पर नशा के खिलाफ आवाज उठाने वालों की सुरक्षा पर फिर से सवाल खड़े हो रहे हैं. हालिया मामला खडूर साहिब विधानसभा क्षेत्र के गांव डालेके के मोड़ पर दिनदहाड़े फायरिंग की घटना ने लोगों को डरा दिया है. जानकारी के अनुसार, यहां पर आम आदमी पार्टी से जुड़ी महिला सरपंच मंजीत कौर के पति सुखबीर सिंह पर हमलावरों ने गोली चला दी.
हालांकि, गनीमत रही कि होली सुखबीर सिंह को छूकर निकल गई, जिससे वह जख्मी हो गए. उनको उपचार के लिए अस्पताल में भर्ती कराया गया, जहां से उन्हें छुट्टी मिल गई है. इस घटना को लेकर महिला सरपंच ने बताया कि वह अपने पति के साथ एटीएम जा रही थी. इसी दौरान कुछ बदमाशों ने उनकी बाइक को टक्कर मार दी.
फिर आरोपियों ने उनकी बाइक पर गोली चलाई और फिर हाथापाई शुरू कर दी. सरपंच ने कहा कि हमलावरों ने उनका मोबाइल भी छीन लिय, जिससे वह किसी को मदद के लिए न बुला पाएं. इसके बाद आरोपियों ने फिर से फायरिंग की, जिसमें सुखबीर सिंह गंभीर रूप से जख्मी हो गए. वहीं, हमलावर मौके से फरार हो गए.
घटना को लेकर महिला सरपंच मंजीत कौर ने आरोप लगाया कि गांव में कुछ लोग नशे का कारोबार करके हैं, जिसका वो और उनका परिवार काफी विरोध करता है. सरपंच ने कहा कि हमने पहले भी इस युवक को नशा बेचने से रोका था, जिस कारण परिवार को धमकियां मिल रही थी. अब उनके पति पर जानलेवा हमला हुआ है.
सरपंच का कहना है कि इसी रंजिश के कारण उनके पति को निशाना बनाया गया है. इसके अलावा उन्होंने पुलिस पर भी देरी से पहुंचने का आरोप लगाया. महिला सरपंच ने आरोपियों की जल्दी से गिरफ्तारी और सख्त कार्रवाई की मांग की है. बताया जा रहा है कि इस मामले में पुलिस ने बताया कि गोली लगने के कारण शख्स को गहरा घाव नहीं आया है और मामूली खरोंच आई हैं.
तरनतारन के एसएसपी ने बताया कि दोनों गुटों के बीच काफी पुरानी रंजिश है. पुलिस का कहना है कि सरपंच के पति पर हमला करने के मामले की जांच की जा रही है. मामले में 2 संदिग्धों की तलाश कर ली गई है और इनका आपराधिक रिकॉर्ड भी सामने आया है.

title: 'Sincerely Apologise': Tamil Nadu Govt Apologises To Supreme Court, Says Temple Board Did Not Authorise Team For Deepathoon Ritual
description: The Tamil Nadu government has apologised to the Supreme Court after the Karthigai Deepam was not lit at Thiruparankundram's Deepathoon despite its November 20 order. Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna blamed the temple board's refusal to authorise the team and denied deliberate disobedience.
author: Shruti Sneha
content:
'Sincerely Apologise': Tamil Nadu Govt Apologises To Supreme Court, Says Temple Board Did Not Authorise Team For Deepathoon Ritual
The Tamil Nadu government has apologised to the Supreme Court after the Karthigai Deepam was not lit at Thiruparankundram's Deepathoon despite its November 20 order. Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna blamed the temple board's refusal to authorise the team and denied deliberate disobedience.
- India News
- 4 min read
New Delhi: The Tamil Nadu government has apologized to the Supreme Court for failing to light the Karthigai Deepam at the controversial Deepathoon pillar atop Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai on November 24, even though the Supreme Court's November 20 judgment had allowed the ceremony. Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna stated in a status report submitted to the court that although the administration had made plans to carry out the directives, they were unable to do so because the Board of Trustees of the temple had not approved the group that was suggested to conduct the ceremony.
“I sincerely apologise for the lamp not being lit at the Deepathoon," the Collector said in his affidavit.
A bench consisting of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi was presented with the status report. On behalf of the Collector, Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan told the bench that the ceremonial lamp could not be lit at the summit pillar.
Why Was The Deepathoon Ritual Not Conducted Despite The SC Order?
The Collector gave an explanation of the situation and stated that the district administration has complied with the directives issued by the Supreme Court on November 20. Nevertheless, the suggested team to ignite the lamp at the Deepathoon was rejected by the temple management.
Advertisement
The report states that the Board of Trustees of the temple chose to carry on with the long-standing custom of holding the Karthigai Deepam event at its traditional site.
Additionally, the Collector said that the district administration was unable to independently designate or approve people to carry out a religious rite on behalf of the Devasthanam.
Advertisement
“At no point did the Devasthanam communicate to the District Collector any authorisation of persons to light the lamp at the Deepathoon," the affidavit stated.
The report further said that all administrative preparations had been completed before the scheduled ceremony. The law-and-order situation was reported to be normal at 3 pm on November 24, with a deployment plan involving 5,797 police personnel in place.
Rejecting allegations of deliberate disobedience of the court's directions, Krishna said, “There has been no wilful deliberate disobedience on my part of any directions of this Hon’ble Court. I hold the orders of the Hon’ble Court on highest respect."
He added that the administration had acted in good faith and would submit an additional status report along with supporting documents.
What Happened At Thiruparankundram Hill On November 24?
The controversy revolves around the Deepathoon, a stone pillar located atop Thiruparankundram Hill. On November 20, the Supreme Court issued an interim ruling allowing a limited team approved by the temple administration to light the Karthigai Deepam ceremonially at the contested pillar.
On November 24, however, the ceremony was held in the customary site close to the Uchipillaiyar Temple rather than the Deepathoon.
At around six o'clock in the evening, a crew authorized by the temple and police officers lighted the lamp at the Deepam Mandapam, which is close to the Uchipillaiyar Temple.
The Deepam was lighted in the Deepa Mandapam, near the Uchipillaiyar Temple, above the temple of the ruling god, Lord Subramania Swamy, according to Tamil Nadu Law Minister R Nirmal Kumar.
What Happens Next In The Karthigai Deepam Case?
The Supreme Court has asked the parties to file appropriate applications and indicated that it would examine the developments surrounding the non-implementation of its November 20 order.
The main plea challenging the Madras High Court order permitting the ceremonial lighting of the lamp has been scheduled for final hearing in January 2027.
The bench may also consider a contempt petition over the alleged failure to comply with its directions. A contempt petition has been initiated against the Madurai District Collector and three other officials in connection with the incident.
The Collector has maintained that there was no wilful violation of the court's order and has assured the court that an additional status report, along with supporting documents, will be submitted.

title: 'Not Today': SC Defers Interim Bail For Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam In 2020 Delhi Riots Conspiracy Case, Seeks Delhi Police Response
description: The Supreme Court has sought the Delhi Police's response to bail pleas filed by Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case. The bench declined interim relief for now, with lawyers citing prolonged incarceration and delays in the examination of witnesses.
author: Shruti Sneha
content:
'Not Today': SC Defers Interim Bail For Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam In 2020 Delhi Riots Conspiracy Case, Seeks Delhi Police Response
The Supreme Court has sought the Delhi Police's response to bail pleas filed by Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case. The bench declined interim relief for now, with lawyers citing prolonged incarceration and delays in the examination of witnesses.
- India News
- 3 min read
New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Wednesday, November 25, declined to grant interim bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) case linked to the alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots. However, in response to their pleas contesting the Delhi High Court's September 30 judgment granting them bail, the court sent letters to the Delhi Police.
The case was considered by a three-judge panel that included Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi, and V Mohana. Senior attorneys for both Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam pushed for temporary relief, but the bench said "Not today" and refused to take their demands into consideration.
Before addressing the motions for temporary bail, the court stated that it will first review Delhi Police's response. It also directed that the matter be placed before the Chief Justice of India on the administrative side for the constitution of a three-judge bench to hear the case.
Why Did Umar Khalid And Sharjeel Imam Seek Interim Bail?
Senior attorney Kapil Sibal, representing Umar Khalid, asked for temporary bail at the hearing while the primary petitions were still pending. Sharjeel Imam's attorney, senior advocate Siddharth Dave, also requested a similar remedy, citing the activist's protracted detention as an undertrial.
Advertisement
Both campaigners have contested the Delhi High Court's decision to refuse them bail, claiming that despite their extended detention, the trial has not advanced far.
Imam emphasized in his petition that the case's chargesheet was submitted on September 25, 2020. The prosecution has listed almost 900 witnesses, including 47 protected witnesses, and 18 accused are on trial.
Advertisement
Imam further submitted that despite spending six years and nine months in custody as an undertrial, the prosecution had not examined even a single witness.
Khalid, meanwhile, cited the non-examination of protected witnesses and argued that the one-year embargo imposed by the Supreme Court was nearing its end. According to his plea, allowing the embargo to expire without progress in the trial would make his continued incarceration a violation of his fundamental right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution.
What Did The Delhi High Court Rule Earlier?
The Supreme Court proceedings follow the Delhi High Court's September 30 decision rejecting the bail applications of both activists in the UAPA case.
The duo subsequently approached the top court, challenging the High Court's refusal to grant them relief and seeking consideration of their prolonged detention and the pace of the trial.
The Supreme Court has now sought the Delhi Police's response before deciding whether interim bail can be considered.
What Is The February 2020 Delhi Riots Conspiracy Case?
The case concerns an alleged larger conspiracy behind the violence that broke out in northeast Delhi in February 2020 during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), 2019, and the proposed National Register of Citizens (NRC).
Sharjeel Imam was arrested in connection with the case on August 25, 2020, while Umar Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020. Both have remained in custody since their arrests.
The prosecution has accused them of involvement in the alleged conspiracy behind the violence, with the case being investigated under the stringent provisions of the UAPA.
The latest Supreme Court proceedings concern their challenge to the denial of bail and their request for interim release while the legal process continues.

title: 'Govt Acted Correctly, Prevented Major Disturbance': Dargah Secretary Defends Tamil Nadu's Karthigai Deepam Decision Amid Row
description: Arif Khan, Secretary of the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Dargah, defended the Tamil Nadu government's decision to light the Karthigai Deepam near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple, citing Agama traditions and long-standing practices amid the Thiruparankundram controversy.
author: Asian News International
content:
'Govt Acted Correctly, Prevented Major Disturbance': Dargah Secretary Defends Tamil Nadu's Karthigai Deepam Decision Amid Row
Arif Khan, Secretary of the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Dargah, defended the Tamil Nadu government's decision to light the Karthigai Deepam near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple, citing Agama traditions and long-standing practices amid the Thiruparankundram controversy.
- India News
- 4 min read
Madurai: Amid the ongoing controversy over the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at Thiruparankundram Hill, Arif Khan, Secretary of the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Dargah, on Wednesday defended the Tamil Nadu government's decision, saying the lamp was lit at its usual location in accordance with the temple's Agama traditions and long-standing practices.
Speaking to ANI on the issue, Khan said it was incorrect to claim that the state government had not lit the lamp, and appreciated its handling of the law-and-order situation to prevent religious clashes and communal divisions.
"It is not correct to say that the Tamil Nadu government did not light the lamp. The lamp was lit. In accordance with the temple's Agama traditions and long-standing practices, the government ensured that the lamp was lit at its usual location near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple atop Thiruparankundram Hill. There has been no deviation from the established practice," he said.
Thanking the state government for its handling of the situation, Khan said the authorities had taken a clear stand after considering the legal and religious aspects of the matter.
Advertisement
"I would like to thank the Tamil Nadu government for handling the law-and-order situation effectively and preventing any religious clashes or communal divisions in the state. The government took a clear and decisive stand. The authorities are well aware of the law. If the Tamil Nadu government has taken such a decision, it would certainly have considered all the legal aspects before doing so," he said.
He further said that temple priests had held consultations on the proposed arrangement before arriving at a decision.
Advertisement
"The government also considered the Agama requirements governing the lighting of the lamp. Even yesterday afternoon, the temple priests held consultations to determine whether the proposed arrangement was appropriate. Only after considering all these aspects did they arrive at a decision. They have also issued a statement today," Khan said.
Emphasising that the government had prevented a potentially major disturbance in the state, he said, "The government has acted correctly. Most importantly, it has prevented a potentially major disturbance in Tamil Nadu. That is what we appreciate. The government has discharged its responsibility properly. There is no question of the government violating the law. It has simply followed the established practice that has been observed for generations."
The remarks come amid a political and religious controversy over the non-lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram Hill, despite the Supreme Court's interim order directing that the lamp be lit there.
The Maha Deepam was instead lit near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple as part of the annual Karthigai Deepam festival on Tuesday, while police personnel were deployed near the Deepathoon ahead of the scheduled ceremony.
BJP leader Sudhanshu Trivedi, earlier in the day, accused the Tamil Nadu government and the INDIA bloc of failing to comply with the Supreme Court's order.
Addressing a press conference, Trivedi alleged that the state government had not implemented the court's direction permitting the ceremonial lighting of the lamp at the disputed hilltop pillar for one day, subject to certain conditions.
He also questioned Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the issue, alleging that the INDIA bloc's position contradicted its stated commitment to protecting the Constitution.
Trivedi further criticised the detentions made during the protests and questioned whether the state machinery would take similar action against Muslim clerics during Eid festivities.
Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) International President Alok Kumar also condemned the Tamil Nadu government, alleging that denying permission to light the Maha Deepam at the sacred hill amounted to defiance of the Supreme Court's order and hurt the religious sentiments of devotees.
"The Hindu society will certainly respond democratically, at the appropriate time, to this mindset that hurts the sentiments of devotees and commits contempt of the Judiciary," he said.
Kumar alleged that the state government's decision amounted to challenging the judiciary and the Constitution, and expressed confidence that the Supreme Court would take action against those who had allegedly defied its order.
Meanwhile, Madurai Police, earlier in the day, said cases had been registered against around 300 BJP and Hindu organisation members for staging protests in Thiruparankundram on Tuesday, demanding that the lamp be lit at the Deepathoon.
According to police, cases were registered under six sections, including unlawful assembly without permission, causing a breach of public peace, making controversial remarks and obstructing government servants from discharging their duties.
The protests followed the lighting of the Maha Deepam near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple instead of the Deepathoon, despite the Supreme Court's interim direction.

title: Tracks of trust: How India is using railways to bring its neighbours closer
description: From a 1927 narrow-gauge line in the Nepal Terai to the new Ayodhya-Janakpur Sarayu-Kamala Express, India’s rail diplomacy with Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Myanmar is a win-win wager on trade, pilgrims and people-to-people ties
author: Akhileshwar Sahay
content:
Tracks of trust: How India is using railways to bring its neighbours closer
From a 1927 narrow-gauge line in the Nepal Terai to the new Ayodhya-Janakpur Sarayu-Kamala Express, India’s rail diplomacy with Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Myanmar is a win-win wager on trade, pilgrims and people-to-people ties
On Monday (November 23), Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah flagged off the inaugural Sarayu-Kamala Express between Ayodhya and Janakpur. Named after the river of Ram's city and the river of Sita's Mithila, the weekly train covers 604 kilometres, stopping at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur and Basti, leaving Janakpur Dham on Saturdays and Ayodhya Cantt on Mondays.
It was Shah's first visit to India since he was sworn in as prime minister in March 2026. The joint press release records eight MoUs, Indian development assistance of Rs 15,000 crore, and a new route for Nepal's transit trade through Deendayal Port at Kandla, with access to Paradip to follow once the infrastructure is in place. On rail, they closed the survey stage of the Raxaul–Kathmandu line and agreed to collaborate on Nepal's East–West Railway.
Indian Railways pitches the train to pilgrims and to border families in Bihar and Nepal travelling for work, study, and kinship. Behind that sits a larger idea: India is using its railways, the subcontinent's oldest connective tissue, as an instrument of foreign policy.
The idea is not new; the speed and deliberateness are.
The roots: When railways ran before borders hardened
Railways reached the Himalayan kingdom long before diplomacy thought of them. In 1927, Nepal's first railway opened between Amlekhganj and Raxaul on the Indian frontier. It was a two-foot-six-inch narrow-gauge line that ran up from the border through Birgunj, and for years it was, in effect, Kathmandu's gateway to India. In 1937, a second line opened from Jaynagar in Bihar to Janakpur.
Both lines began on Indian soil, at Raxaul and Jaynagar, and fed into the railway network of British India, carrying timber, goods and passengers. They were built in the Rana era with British engineering and survey help, but they ran as Nepalese railways, not as part of British India's state railway system. Passenger service on the Raxaul–Amlekhganj line ended in 1965, and freight wound down later in the decade. The decisive blow came from the road: the Tribhuvan Rajpath, opened in 1956, shifted traffic to Kathmandu to buses and trucks, and air links further changed travel.
The Janakpur line survived as a rickety lifeline on ageing track. The stretch beyond Janakpur to Bijalpura was cut in 2001 after flood damage, and the rest closed in early 2014 for conversion to broad gauge, reopening in phases.
To the east, history was crueller. Undivided Bengal had an integrated rail network. The 1947 Partition split it across a new border, though cross-border trains kept running until the 1965 India–Pakistan war halted passenger services. Partition also severed Assam's rail route through East Pakistan; India answered with the Assam Rail Link through North Bengal, begun in January 1948 and built in two years, opening to goods in December 1949 and to passengers on January 26, 1950. When the Maitree Express rolled into Dhaka on Pohela Boishakh, April 14, 2008, it restored the Kolkata–Dhaka passenger link after 43 years.
South Asia's railways were built for one economic space that borders fragmented and wars severed. Rail diplomacy today is largely an effort to repair what geography intended and politics undid.
Nepal: From survey files to running trains
For a long time, India-Nepal rail cooperation was more promise than performance. That has changed in the last four years.
On April 2, 2022, Modi and then Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba launched the 35-km Jaynagar-Kurtha cross-border rail link, the first broad-gauge passenger link between two countries and the converted descendant of the 1937 Janakpur line. Modi said the two leaders had agreed to give priority to trade and cross-border connectivity "in all respects", and that the Jayanagar–Kurtha line was part of this. On June 1, 2023, the two prime ministers inaugurated the Jogbani–Biratnagar link in eastern Nepal, built with Indian grant assistance.
The real breakthrough was in freight. On November 13, 2025, the two countries exchanged a Letter of Exchange amending the Protocol to the Treaty of Transit.
It permits rail freight between Jogbani and Biratnagar, including bulk cargo; liberalises Kolkata-Jogbani, Kolkata-Nautanwa, and Visakhapatnam-Nautanwa corridors; and allows containerised and bulk cargo to move by rail directly from Kolkata and Visakhapatnam ports to the Nepal Customs Yard near Biratnagar.
In July 2026, the first direct commercial container train, carrying 40 containers of canola, ran from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar with no transhipment at the border. Until then, Nepal's rail cargo had been funnelled through Birgunj; the transit rights it rides on go back to the Treaty of Trade and Transit of 1960.
Then there is Kathmandu. On April 7, 2018, PMs Modi and Oli agreed to build a new electrified rail line, with India's financial support, from Raxaul to Kathmandu, with India to complete the preparatory survey within a year and its implementation and funding to be settled on the basis of a Detailed Project Report. An MoU for the survey was signed that August on the margins of the Bimstec summit in Kathmandu, with Konkan Railway entrusted with the work. The Final Location Survey report was handed over to Nepal in June 2023, and on November 23 Modi and Shah announced its finalisation. Construction across the Mahabharat and Chure ranges will be a true test of engineering and political will.
East–West Railway adds a second axis. Nepal has long wanted a line running the length of its Terai, from Mechi in the east to Mahakali in the west. At the June 2026 meetings of the bilateral Project Steering Committee and Joint Working Group, two sides discussed Indian technical support, the Raxaul–Kathmandu survey report, and operating procedures for the Janakpur–Ayodhya service. Joined up, a Terai trunk line with spurs to Jaynagar, Raxaul, Jogbani and Nautanwa, plus a climb to Kathmandu, would put every major Nepali town a single journey from an Indian port, pilgrimage centre or city. The Sarayu-Kamala Express is the first visible thread of that network.
Bhutan: The kingdom without a railway gets two
Bhutan has never had a railway. On September 29, 2025, India and Bhutan signed an intergovernmental MoU to establish railway links: Kokrajhar–Gelephu (69 km) and Banarhat–Samtse (20 km), at an estimated cost of Rs 4,033 crore. The first runs from Assam to Gelephu, the site of King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck's Gelephu Mindfulness City, a service-sector special administrative region that India has pledged to support fully. The second runs from West Bengal's Jalpaiguri district to Samtse, Bhutan's industrial town. India will fund both: the Ministry of Railways will pay for the Indian sections, and the Ministry of External Affairs will pay for the Bhutanese sections under India's assistance to Bhutan's 13th Five-Year Plan. The Kokrajhar–Gelephu line has been declared a Special Railway Project to speed up land acquisition.
At the special MEA briefing announcing the lines, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw put the logic plainly: by building about 70 km, Bhutan gains access to a 150,000-km network. India accounts for nearly 80 per cent of Bhutan's total trade. For a landlocked kingdom, a railhead at its own border cuts the cost of everything from cement to fuel; for Assam's Bodoland region, it turns a peripheral district into a gateway.
Bangladesh: The network built, the trains stopped
Bangladesh is where India's rail diplomacy has gone furthest, and where it has stumbled hardest.
After Maitree, came the Kolkata–Khulna Bandhan Express, flagged off in November 2017, and the Mitali Express to New Jalpaiguri in 2022. In all, six pre-1965 rail links between the two countries have been restored. On November 1, 2023, Modi and Sheikh Hasina inaugurated the Akhaura–Agartala link, the first rail link between Bangladesh and India's Northeast, built with an Indian grant of Rs 392.52 crore, together with the 65-km Khulna–Mongla port rail line, also built with Indian assistance. The Railway Ministry told the Lok Sabha in December 2015 that the Akhaura link would cut the Kolkata–Agartala rail distance from 1,581 km via Guwahati to about 460 km via Dhaka.
Then came July 2024. Amid the upheaval in Bangladesh, the Maitree, Bandhan and Mitali passenger services were suspended "due to security considerations"; goods trains continue to run. The Maitree had been popular, especially with Bangladeshi travellers coming to India for medical treatment and tourism.
Candour requires saying that this is a setback. Hope allows us to say it is not the end. Bangladesh's BNP won the general election of February 12, 2026, and Modi was among the first leaders to call Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. In September 2026, the two railway administrations met in Dhaka to discuss restoring all three passenger trains, with Dhaka proposing a faster Maitree route over the Padma Bridge. By early October, no resumption date had been announced.
The tracks, the interchange yards and the bridges are still there. That is the quiet virtue of rail diplomacy: physical connectivity outlasts political weather. When governments are ready to talk, the infrastructure is waiting.
Sri Lanka: Rebuilding the line the war destroyed
Sri Lanka's link with India's railways once ran through the sea. The Indo-Ceylon Boat Mail carried passengers from Madras Egmore over the Pamban Bridge to Dhanushkodi, across the Palk Strait by ferry to Talaimannar, and on by train to Colombo, until the December 1964 cyclone destroyed the Dhanushkodi line.
Modern rail diplomacy with Colombo has been about rebuilding. The Northern line to Jaffna, Kankesanthurai and Talaimannar was destroyed in the civil war. IRCON rebuilt it under a concessional Indian line of credit of about $800 million, and Modi flagged off the restored service at Talaimannar Pier in March 2015. On April 6, 2025, he and President Anura Kumara Dissanayake inaugurated the 128-km Maho–Omanthai line, refurbished with $91.27 million of Indian assistance, and launched a Maho–Anuradhapura signalling system funded by a $14.89 million Indian grant. The same day, Modi opened the new Pamban Bridge in Tamil Nadu.
Trains now run to Talaimannar on one side of the strait and to Rameswaram on the other, but no rail-and-ferry service yet joins them.
Myanmar: The gateway still to be built
Myanmar is India's land gateway to Southeast Asia and the Trans-Asian Railway. The Railway Ministry told the Lok Sabha in 2016 that the missing link is about 360 km, from Jiribam in India to Kalay in Myanmar, via Moreh and Tamu; Imphal-Moreh accounts for 111 km and Tamu-Kalay for 128 km. A final location survey for the Imphal-Moreh section was sanctioned in January 2022. In Mizoram, the 223-km Sairang–Hbicchhuah line aims to take tracks to the state's southern border, opening trade routes to Myanmar and Southeast Asia via Sittwe port.
Since the 2021 coup and civil war, neither side has been able to build across the frontier. Myanmar is rail diplomacy in waiting. India is wise to keep laying track towards the border, so that when Myanmar is ready, the line ends at Moreh rather than in Imphal.
Why it is a win-win
Critics see only a contest of influence with China; that reading is incomplete. Rail diplomacy works because each side gains something real.
For Nepal and Bhutan, it corrects geography. Being landlocked is a tax on every import and export. A direct container train from Kolkata, port access at Kandla and Paradip, and railheads at Biratnagar, Gelephu, and Samtse lower that tax. Cheaper inputs make Nepali and Bhutanese manufacturing more competitive, and a reliable outlet to the sea gives them leverage in third-country markets.
For India, it is a stable and prosperous periphery. Every container that moves by rail to Biratnagar is cargo for Indian ports, Indian Railways and Indian logistics firms. The Northeast, long a cul-de-sac reached only through the narrow Siliguri corridor, gains alternative routes through Bangladesh.
For land trade, rail is the efficient mode. Trucks queuing for days at border points such as Raxaul-Birgunj and Petrapole-Benapole are among South Asia's most familiar images of lost money. A rake of 40 containers replaces dozens of trucks, cuts handling and spoilage, and simplifies customs. The November 2025 transit amendment and the July 2026 Kolkata–Biratnagar run show what happens when procedure catches up with infrastructure.
For people-to-people ties, it is the cheapest bridge there is. The Ayodhya–Janakpur train is a Ramayana pilgrimage circuit, but it is also a family train. The roti-beti relationship of the Terai and Mithila, with marriages, festivals and shared kin on both sides of the open border, runs on affordable, predictable travel. The same was true of the Maitree Express, whose passengers were overwhelmingly ordinary Bangladeshi travellers, patients and tourists. Air travel is for the few; trains are for the many.
For the region, it is integration by stealth. The Bhutan lines plug into the same Indian grid that carries Nepal's freight and once carried Bangladesh's passengers; a line to Moreh would one day carry it towards Southeast Asia. That is regionalism built from the ground up rather than declared at summits.
The caveats India must heed
Rail diplomacy will be judged by trains that run, not by MoUs signed. The remaining sections of the Jaynagar-Bijalpura-Bardibas and Jogbani-Biratnagar links, both funded by Indian grants, were still under implementation in June 2026. The Raxaul–Kathmandu line, announced in 2018, has only now finished its survey. The Imphal–Moreh line is still under survey, and Bangladesh's passenger trains have been idle for more than two years.
Three things would help: published, deadline-bound joint monitoring; customs, immigration and visa regimes reformed alongside the tracks, since a train held a day at the border loses its advantage; and insulating passenger services from political turbulence, so that people with no stake in a diplomatic quarrel do not lose their train home.
The track ahead
Nearly a century after a narrow-gauge steam train first puffed out of Raxaul towards Amlekhganj, India and Nepal are planning a broad-gauge electric line to Kathmandu. Bhutan is about to hear its first train whistle. Bangladesh and India are working out how to bring passengers back, Sri Lanka's war-torn Northern line is running again on Indian credit, and the track to Myanmar waits at the edge of Manipur.
The rail lines of South Asia were laid for one economic space. Politics divided it; diplomacy, patiently, is sewing it back together. If India keeps its timelines and its neighbours keep the trains running, the Sarayu-Kamala Express will be remembered not as a ceremonial flag-off but as one more stitch in a subcontinent learning, once again, to travel together.
(Akhileshwar Sahay is a Multidisciplinary Thought Leader with Action Bias, a Bharat-based Impact Consultant and a keen watcher of the changing national and international scenario. Views are personal.)

title: India opens doors to prized missile test range for Japan for first time, hypersonics collaboration on cards
description: Japan was once a military force constitutionally constrained to an exclusively defensive role. However, it is now gradually becoming a force with long-range strike capabilities, an expanding defence industry and a much greater role in Indo-Pacific security
author: Snehesh Alex Philip
content:
India opens doors to prized missile test range for Japan for first time, hypersonics collaboration on cards
Japan was once a military force constitutionally constrained to an exclusively defensive role. However, it is now gradually becoming a force with long-range strike capabilities, an expanding defence industry and a much greater role in Indo-Pacific security
In a major shift in India's defence cooperation policy, New Delhi is preparing to open up its most prized missile-testing facility to a foreign country for the first time, allowing Japan to use the Defence Research and Development Organisation's (DRDO) Integrated Test Range (ITR) at Chandipur in Odisha for its missile programme.
Not just Chandipur, India is also open to allowing Japan access to two upcoming state-of-the-art testing facilities in West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh, government sources told Firstpost.
The move goes beyond providing testing infrastructure. The two countries are also exploring the possibility of sharing technical know-how and collaborating on advanced missile programmes, including hypersonic weapons, sources said.
They added that India and Japan are also looking at cooperating on the shipbuilding front, especially warships. Sources clarified that, contrary to reports of plans to build Mogani-class multi-mission stealth frigates in India, both sides are working on sharing technical know-how and design features.
India has offered its shipyards and defence PSUs to Japan for collaboration, as well as manufacturing for Tokyo itself and exports from India.
Sources explained that manufacturing in India will be cheaper for Japan, and that this is something under discussion. For example, plans are not just to manufacture the Unicorn (Unified Complex Radio Antenna) for the Indian Navy's requirements but also for exports by Japan itself.
These were among the key issues discussed during the India-Japan 2+2 dialogue last week, led by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar.
Following the meeting, the two countries signed a Letter of Intent (LoI) on the utilisation of firing ranges in India.
Why Japan is keen for Indian firing ranges
Under the arrangement, Japan's Self-Defence Forces will, for the first time, be able to conduct live-fire training in India, including trials involving surface-to-ship missiles such as the Type-25, a next-generation anti-ship missile with a reported range of around 1,000 km.
Both sides will now work towards accelerating coordination between their respective defence authorities to operationalise the arrangement at the earliest. Japan is also in talks with Australia for the test ranges.
Japan is undergoing one of the most significant transformations in its military posture since the Second World War.
What was once a military force constitutionally constrained to an exclusively defensive role is gradually becoming a force with long-range strike capabilities, an expanding defence industry and a much greater role in Indo-Pacific security.
Sources said a Japanese military team had visited India in October to assess various missile-testing facilities. The team spent about a week examining potential ranges where Japan could conduct missile trials as well as test its small attack drones.
Japan faces geographical constraints at home, particularly in identifying sufficiently large and safe maritime corridors for long-range missile firing. India's eastern coastline, with its established missile-testing infrastructure and access to the Bay of Bengal, offers an attractive alternative.
Sources said the discussions are not limited to access to testing facilities. India and Japan are also looking at sharing technical expertise and exploring opportunities for collaboration in advanced weapons programmes, particularly hypersonic technologies.
Japan is seeking to develop a multi-layered coastal defence system incorporating large numbers of relatively inexpensive unmanned aerial, surface and underwater vehicles for reconnaissance and attack missions.
These capabilities would complement its growing arsenal of stand-off missiles, which are designed to strike targets from outside an adversary's engagement range.
Tokyo is developing a new generation of missiles to strengthen deterrence against China's growing military activity around its periphery and respond to North Korea's increasingly sophisticated missile arsenal.
Why the Integrated Test Range matters
The Integrated Test Range at Chandipur is among India's most strategically important defence-testing facilities. It is a critical part of the country's missile-development ecosystem, providing the infrastructure required to launch, track and validate advanced missile systems.
Its capabilities include sophisticated radars, telemetry systems, electro-optical tracking equipment and mission-control infrastructure, which allow DRDO scientists to monitor missile trajectories and assess their performance during flight trials.
The facility has played an important role in testing several Indian missile systems, including air-defence and ballistic missile defence interceptors.
Opening up such infrastructure to Japan would mark a significant expansion of bilateral defence cooperation, taking the relationship beyond joint military exercises and conventional defence technology partnerships, sources said.

title: Dalai Lama gets Lutyens' Delhi bungalow as India gives his office a permanent base in capital
description: The Dalai Lama will continue to be based in Dharamshala, but his office now has a dedicated facility in Lutyens' Delhi for official engagements
author: FP News Desk
content:
Dalai Lama gets Lutyens' Delhi bungalow as India gives his office a permanent base in capital
The Dalai Lama will continue to be based in Dharamshala, but his office now has a dedicated facility in Lutyens' Delhi for official engagements
The Indian government has allotted a bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi to the office of the 14th Dalai Lama, giving the Tibetan spiritual leader a dedicated base in the national capital for his visits and official engagements.
The property, located at 20 Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane, has been allotted to the Gaden Phodrang Trust, which serves as the Dalai Lama's official office and manages his spiritual and humanitarian work.
The allotment followed a request from the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), as per news agency PTI. While the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry has not issued an official statement, government accommodation of this kind is generally allotted for three years, with the possibility of an extension.
Security upgrades worth nearly Rs 35 lakh are being carried out at the property. These include reinforced gates, a security cabin and additional protective structures along the boundary wall. The work is intended to strengthen security and regulate access to the premises.
Why does the Dalai Lama need a base in Delhi?
The Dalai Lama's primary residence is in McLeod Ganj, near Dharamshala in Himachal Pradesh, where he has lived since fleeing Tibet in 1959.
He escaped Tibet amid a Chinese crackdown and unrest in Lhasa, eventually reaching India on March 31, 1959. New Delhi granted him asylum, beginning a relationship that has continued for more than six decades. India has since been home to the Dalai Lama and a large Tibetan refugee community.
Although he is based in Dharamshala, the Dalai Lama travels to the national capital for meetings, engagements and other official work. Having a dedicated facility in Delhi is expected to reduce the logistical challenges involved in arranging accommodation and security for him and his staff.
The new bungalow will also provide his office with a permanent base from which to coordinate engagements and its work on Tibetan culture, humanitarian causes and interfaith dialogue.
What is the Gaden Phodrang Trust?
The bungalow has been allotted to the Gaden Phodrang Trust rather than to the Dalai Lama as a private residence.
Gaden Phodrang is the official office of the Dalai Lama. It was registered as a private trust in India in 2011, after he voluntarily gave up his political authority in favour of an elected Tibetan leadership.
The trust is dedicated to preserving the institution of the Dalai Lama and supporting his spiritual and humanitarian work. Its stated commitments include promoting human values, encouraging interfaith harmony, preserving Tibetan culture and identity, protecting the environment and promoting a deeper understanding of ancient Indian wisdom.
The distinction is important: the new facility is intended to support the institution and office of the Dalai Lama, not to shift his residence from Dharamshala to Delhi.
Tibetan leadership welcomes India's move
The allotment has been welcomed by the Tibetan leadership in exile.
Dolma Tsering, Speaker of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, expressed gratitude to the Indian government, saying the accommodation would make the Dalai Lama's visits to the capital more convenient and provide greater comfort and security during his stays.
'This is very welcome news. The accommodation will make His Holiness the Dalai Lama's visits to the national capital far more convenient and provide greater comfort and security during his stays in New Delhi,' she said as cited by news agency ANI.
Choedak Gyatso, a member of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile's standing committee, also welcomed the decision, describing it as a reaffirmation of India's longstanding support for the Tibetan people.
The next Dalai Lama and the battle over who gets to choose
The allotment also comes amid growing international attention on the Dalai Lama's succession, with a US congressional panel recently urging Washington to coordinate with New Delhi on the process.
The bipartisan US-China Economic and Security Review Commission has recommended that the US recognise the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole authority to identify his successor and reject any candidate selected or appointed by Beijing.
It has also called for intelligence-sharing and contingency planning with India, warning that China could use political pressure, cyber operations and disinformation to influence the succession.

title: Bollywood union asks PM Modi to bar Netflix's Pakistani series in India
description: The All Indian Cine Workers Association has sought a permanent law barring Pakistani content on Indian screens ahead of the December 4 release of Netflix's first Urdu-language series
author: Reuters
content:
Bollywood union asks PM Modi to bar Netflix's Pakistani series in India
The All Indian Cine Workers Association has sought a permanent law barring Pakistani content on Indian screens ahead of the December 4 release of Netflix's first Urdu-language series
Listen to This Article
A prominent Bollywood workers' union has asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government to ban a forthcoming Pakistani series on Netflix in India, while seeking a law prohibiting content from its foe from being shown in the country.
The first ‌part of "Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo" (All the Love Our Hearts Carry) is scheduled to air on Netflix on December 4 and is the global streaming giant's first Urdu-language series. Several top Pakistani actors feature in it.
"No Pakistani face, voice or story has a place on Indian screens," the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA), a union of film workers, said in a letter addressed to Modi late on Tuesday.
Netflix and a Modi spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
New Delhi has for decades accused Islamabad of aiding, abetting and orchestrating violent attacks by Islamist militant groups ‌across India, including one on Hindu tourists in Indian Kashmir last year that killed 26 people and led to the worst fighting between the neighbours in years. Pakistan denies India's accusations.
Also Read
India has asked all streaming platforms to stop screening Pakistani shows, many of which enjoy a huge fan following in the country, after ‌the fighting, and AICWA said Netflix would be in violation of the advisory if ‌it showed the series.
Pakistani content is not screened on streaming platforms in India, though several ‌series are available on YouTube.
Several of the actors in the series had spoken out against India during times of tension between the two countries, AICWA, which says it is the largest union of film workers, said in the letter.
"We have also demanded a strong, permanent law with the severest penalties and we appeal to Netflix India and all OTT platforms never to show any Pakistani content in India," it said.
India ‌is a key market for Netflix, with an estimated 20 million users, according to HSBC, as well ‌as a growing user base of young people with access to cheap internet.
Netflix describes "Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo," which is based on a novel by Pakistani author Farhat Ishtiaq, as a story of six couples and how they discover love. It stars Fawad Khan, Sanam Saeed, Mahira Khan and others.

title: 1 year on, firms struggle to fully implement 4 labour codes, finds survey
description: A new survey finds that payroll and compliance changes are the biggest implementation challenges, cited by 73.5 per cent of respondents, while 74.4 per cent expect employment costs to rise
author: Barkha Mathur
content:
1 year on, firms struggle to fully implement 4 labour codes, finds survey
A new survey finds that payroll and compliance changes are the biggest implementation challenges, cited by 73.5 per cent of respondents, while 74.4 per cent expect employment costs to rise
Listen to This Article
Just over half of organisations surveyed consider themselves fully prepared to implement India's four labour codes, a year after they came into effect, even as companies continue to grapple with payroll and compliance changes, interpretation of the revised wage definition and pending state-level rules, according to a Grant Thornton Bharat report.
The report, Labour codes: Implementation pulse, released on Wednesday, draws on responses from more than 200 organisations across sectors, including technology, manufacturing, financial services, professional services, education, energy, infrastructure and hospitality.
The survey found that 50.6 per cent of respondents described themselves as fully prepared, while 28.8 per cent were still preparing for implementation. Another 11.7 per cent had not started the process and 9 per cent were not aware of the changes.
However, overall preparedness has not necessarily translated into changes in workplace policies and processes. While 54.3 per cent of respondents had completed an impact assessment of the codes, only 41.9 per cent had reviewed their human resources (HR) policies and employment contracts for gaps.
The four labour codes, which consolidate 29 central labour laws covering wages, social security, industrial relations and occupational safety, came into effect on November 21, 2025.
Also Read
Revised wage definition likely to push up employment costs
About 66.2 per cent of respondents said they had reviewed and updated their salary structures in line with the revised definition, while another 10.5 per cent planned to undertake the exercise. However, 74.4 per cent expected the change to increase employment costs.
The report said that nearly half of respondents, or 49.6 per cent, estimated that employment costs would increase by up to 5 per cent, while 12 per cent expected an increase of more than 5 per cent. Another 12.8 per cent said they did not expect any impact, while an equal proportion could not estimate the effect.
Gratuity was identified as the component most likely to see an increase, with 43.6 per cent of respondents flagging it, followed by provident fund contributions at 30.8 per cent.
The additional cost will require companies to decide how much of the increase they are willing to absorb. While 49.6 per cent of respondents said they planned to absorb it, 29.9 per cent were still evaluating their approach, while 20.5 per cent did not plan to absorb the increase.
Payroll and compliance changes remain biggest hurdles
Although 48.7 per cent of organisations said their payroll software was fully ready, another 31.6 per cent were still upgrading their systems. A further 13.7 per cent said their systems were not ready, while 6 per cent reported technical difficulties linked to the deemed wage provisions.
According to the report, payroll and compliance changes were the leading implementation challenge that 73.5 per cent of respondents flagged, followed by HR policy revisions at 66.7 per cent and legal interpretation of the revised wage definition at 55.6 per cent. Employee communication and technology were cited by 36.8 per cent and 35.9 per cent, respectively.
The requirement to complete full and final settlement of wages within two working days also remains an area of unfinished work. Only 38.8 per cent of respondents said they had implemented the requirement, while 33.1 per cent were discussing its implementation. Another 23.8 per cent considered it impractical, and 4.4 per cent were unaware of the change.
Pending state-level rules are another constraint on implementation. As many as 77.8 per cent of respondents indicated that finalisation of state rules was important for complete readiness. Among them, 43.6 per cent said the absence of final rules had a moderate impact on their readiness, while 34.2 per cent reported a significant impact.
The areas where companies sought further regulatory clarification included the definition of wages and its computation methodology, cited by 24.8 per cent of respondents. Deployment of contractual workers in core activities was flagged by 23.1 per cent, while 19.7 per cent sought clarity on the two-working-day full and final settlement requirement.
Workforce deployment through contractors is also likely to be affected. About 65.8 per cent of respondents expected the labour codes to influence how they deploy contractual workers. The report recommends that companies review workforce classifications, contractor arrangements and agreements with manpower providers, particularly where workers are engaged in activities considered core to an establishment.
Despite these implementation gaps, about 72 per cent of respondents said they were either somewhat or very confident about implementing the codes.

title: No global power wants India to progress, says RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
description: He was speaking at the inauguration of the fifth Padmaa Festival in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
author: Press Trust of India
content:
No global power wants India to progress, says RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
He was speaking at the inauguration of the fifth Padmaa Festival in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
Listen to This Article
Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Wednesday said that no power in the world wants India to progress, as global powers seek to assert their dominance and keep others under pressure, believing in the principle of the 'survival of the fittest'.
He was speaking at the inauguration of the fifth Padmaa Festival in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.
Local organisation Gyanyajnah Foundation has organised the three-day Padmaa Festival, which brings together Padma awardees from diverse fields to interact with people.
Bhagwat said that India wants to help everyone and extends assistance even to nations that hate it.
"No power in the world wants India to progress because they only seek power and believe in the principle of the 'survival of the fittest', keeping everyone under pressure. If India grows, their shops will be shut because India wants to help everyone. India helps even its neighbours who hate it," he said.
Also Read
The RSS chief said the younger generation was free from the influences of slavery.
"If someone speaks genuinely, the youth are prepared to stand behind him. They hate lies and want to make their country great," he said.
Former Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General Anil Chauhan (Retd), who also shared the stage with Bhagwat at the event, said the youth will be the biggest contributors to and beneficiaries of 'Viksit Bharat'.
The inauguration ceremony took place at the Manthan Hall of MIT Campus located on Beed Bypass Road in the city. Interactive sessions involving the Padma Shri awardees will take place at the Manthan Hall from Wednesday afternoon, the organisers have said.
